title: Less wind for Lisbon?
standfirst: Late on Tuesday the press began to report that Storm Charles would pass further south, with less wind for Lisbon. At 07:16 on Wednesday IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange, with gusts up to 120 km/h still warned from 09:00; the red rain warning stands. This is what IPMA has written, what one of its meteorologists said aloud, what the headlines say, what the models in the data room show, and what IPMA's warnings for Lisbon say at the last read.

warnings_in_force.about: The official warnings a story about the storm states first, drawn as the front page draws them: for each kind of weather IPMA's newest message by the time it was sent (cap.json beside this file), saying what IPMA's open-data feed (this file) lists where the two differ; resolved when the page is built and read again in the reader's browser. Never a level of our own.

claims.text: IPMA named the storm CHARLES on Monday 9 November at 13:17, in communiqué no. 1, and said its path and strength carried "elevada incerteza".
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, communiqué no. 1

supports.note: No longer in IPMA's feed: kept from the record of the newsroom that read it at the time.

claims.text: Communiqué no. 2, edited on Tuesday at 17:07, put the centre's most likely path "entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro", a stretch of coast that has Lisbon inside it, with the strongest gusts "no bordo sul da depressão": 100 to 120 km/h, locally up to 140.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, communiqué no. 2

contains: a maior probabilidade será o centro da depressão passar entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro
no bordo sul da depressão as rajadas serão da ordem dos 100 a 120 km/h, podendo ser localmente até 140 km/h
elevada incerteza na trajetória e intensidade

claims.text: IPMA has published no communiqué no. 3: at the last read, no. 2 is still the newest text on Charles in its feed.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's communiqués feed

supports.expect: Chuva, vento e agitação marítima - Depressão CHARLES - Continente e Madeira - Comunicado nº2
IPMA's communiqué is still no. 2 (valid 10 Nov 17:07 to 11 Nov 23:59)

claims.text: IPMA sent the red wind warning for the Lisbon district on Tuesday at 07:18: Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00, "Rajadas até 120 km/h, podendo atingir 140 km/h nos locais mais expostos". It stood until Wednesday morning.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, warning (CAP message through MeteoAlarm)

supports.expect: Rajadas até 120 km/h, podendo atingir 140 km/h nos locais mais expostos.

claims.text: At 21:23 on Tuesday IPMA moved Lisbon's red rain warning three hours earlier, to Wednesday 09:00 to 18:00; the same issue added red rain warnings for Beja and Faro, further south.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, warning (CAP message through MeteoAlarm)

supports.expect: new red rain Beja, Faro 09-18; red rain earlier (09-18) Lisboa, Setúbal

claims.text: At 07:16:30 on Wednesday IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange, and started it three hours earlier: orange, 09:00 to 21:00, "Rajadas até 120 km/h". The clause on 140 km/h in the most exposed places is gone. The message replaces the red one of Tuesday 07:18, and was sent 1 hour 44 minutes before the orange begins. The red rain warning is unchanged: 09:00 to 18:00.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, warnings (a CAP message through MeteoAlarm, PO-01-1932)

contains: sent 1 h 44 min before the new orange begins

claims.text: IPMA's two channels disagreed for more than an hour. Its open-data feed still listed the red wind warning for Lisbon at 08:22 and had the orange one at the 08:45 read: it followed the message of 07:16:30 by between 66 and 88 minutes. On Tuesday night the same feed followed a changed warning at least two hours late. The box at the top of this page reads both channels and says when they differ.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's two feeds, as read by incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis

contains: IPMA's open data still showed red wind at 07:38
lagged the CAP messages by at least 2 h

claims.text: The first report we read of a path further south was not IPMA's: at 22:07 on Tuesday Observador's live blog reported the latest runs of the ECMWF model, with an entry between Setúbal and Sines.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Observador, live blog (reporting a model, quoting nobody)

supports.expect: Modelos já apontam para uma trajetória mais a sul: entre Setúbal e Sines, com impactos no Algarve

claims.text: At 22:35 an IPMA meteorologist, Paula Leitão, told Rádio Observador that the depression "deverá entrar entre a região de Lisboa e o Cabo de São Vicente (Sagres)".
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: an IPMA meteorologist, by voice, as relayed by Observador's live blog

claims.text: On the wind, her words were conditional and kept Lisbon in: "Isto ainda atinge a zona de Lisboa, mas é provável que, se houver formação de ventos muito, muito fortes, não seja na região de Lisboa, mas um pouco mais a sul".
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: an IPMA meteorologist, by voice, as relayed by Observador's live blog

claims.text: RTP's Antena 1 carried the shift under IPMA's name in its 22:00 bulletin, published at 22:22; the bulletin is audio and was not heard by us, so who spoke is not recorded.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: RTP (the title of an audio bulletin)

supports.expect: 22h IPMA depressão mudou a trajetória mais para sul

claims.text: By 23:54 the wind was in a headline as a statement: Expresso's "Depressão Charles muda trajetória para sul, com menos vento em Lisboa e Norte mais resguardado".
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Expresso (headline)

supports.expect: Depressão Charles muda trajetória para sul, com menos vento em Lisboa e Norte mais resguardado

claims.text: Others followed: Público's live blog ("Charles passa mais a sul do que o previsto e vento deverá ser menos intenso"), Observador ("IPMA admite que Charles entre mais a sul do que o previsto") and, in a video title, CNN Portugal ("Tempestade chega a Lisboa com menos intensidade do que o previsto").
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Público, Observador, CNN Portugal (headlines and titles)

claims.text: At the reads that found those headlines, IPMA's own channels had not moved: the communiqué was still no. 2 and Lisbon's red warnings stood.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's feeds, as read beside the headlines

claims.text: The line was still running at 03:00 on Wednesday: RTP's radio bulletin is titled "IPMA: depressão Charles vai atingir mais o sul do país". The bulletin was not heard by us. At the same hour IPMA's warnings for Lisbon were unchanged and its communiqué was still no. 2.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: RTP Antena 1 (the title of an audio bulletin)

claims.text: IPMA's own hourly model for Lisbon has moved twice between our reads. On Tuesday evening, under an unchanged stamp, Wednesday's strongest mean wind went from 48.6 km/h at 18:00 to 23.4 km/h at 20:00. At the 08:45 read on Wednesday it was 40 km/h at 14:00, from the south.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: IPMA's automatic hourly forecast for Lisbon (a model's output, not a warning)

supports.note: The run as last read before it was replaced.

claims.text: MET Norway's forecast for Lisbon, at its update of 08:21 on Wednesday, has the strongest mean wind at 55.1 km/h at 15:00, from the south-south-west, and the lowest pressure, 988.8 hPa, in the same hour; this block carries no gusts.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: MET Norway, Locationforecast 2.0 (a second model, never merged with IPMA)

supports.note: The model's own update time, as it stands at each build; the sentence is pinned to the values, not to this stamp.

claims.text: Open-Meteo's forecast for the same point is far lower, and moved again between reads: its strongest mean wind is now 19.4 km/h, at 10:00, and its strongest gust 50 km/h, at 11:00, both from the south. At 14:00 it has 17.6 km/h from the north-east.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Open-Meteo, best match (a second model, never merged with IPMA)

claims.text: The airport's forecast, written by IPMA for pilots, has not eased since: the one issued at 05:00 on Wednesday keeps 30 knots gusting 45 (83 km/h) at times, now from 09:00 to 18:00 (the 23:00 issue ended that at 16:00), with a 30% chance of gusts of 58 knots (107 km/h) in thunderstorms between 10:00 and 18:00.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, the TAF for Lisbon airport (a point forecast for pilots, not a public warning)

claims.text: So the three models in the data room do not agree with each other: the strongest mean wind for Lisbon on Wednesday is 40, 55.1 or 19.4 km/h, at 14:00, 15:00 or 10:00, depending on which is read. IPMA's and MET Norway's are now an hour apart on when, and 15 km/h apart on how strong. None of these is a gust at an exposed place, which is what the warning's 120 km/h measures.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: this desk, setting three files side by side

supports.note: The data room's own note: the airport's gusts and the warning's gusts "are not the same measure"; second models are kept one block per source, "never merged with IPMA".

claims.text: Our meteorologist's first hypothesis, written at 00:05 on Wednesday, was that the centre passes very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00, more likely just south of the city. At 02:35 the meteorologist re-weighed it: "just south of Lisbon" is now held with low confidence (it was medium).
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: low (was medium), for "just south of Lisbon"
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.expect: CHARLES's centre passes very close to Lisbon about 17:00-18:00 Wed, more likely just south of it (further south than the Tuesday-morning guidance)

claims.text: Its guidance for a headline changed with it, and held until the warning was lowered (see the last sentence of this section): "'less wind for Lisbon' is not supported; say the models disagree on which side the centre passes, and IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon stand".
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: the analysis's own guidance, on low confidence about the side and medium about the timing
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.expect: 'less wind for Lisbon' is not supported; say the models disagree on which side the centre passes, and IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon stand

supports.note: The earlier guidance, kept as written.

claims.text: Why: the inputs moved. MET Norway's run of 01:19 has the wind veering through south and south-west to west, its strongest mean wind at 14:00 to 15:00 and its lowest pressure at 15:00, with no swing to north; the airport forecast also veers through south to west. IPMA's older hourly run and its forecasters' words on radio lean the other way. In the analysis's words: "the side is unsettled".
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: low, on which side of Lisbon the centre passes
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.note: The later update of 08:21 on Wednesday still has the wind from the west at 17:00 (274.9 degrees; the run of 01:19 had 283.1).

claims.text: What the re-weighed analysis holds across all its inputs: the centre passes very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00 on Wednesday.
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.expect: centre passes very close to Lisbon between ~15:00 and 18:00 (confidence medium)

claims.text: Set side by side: the headline said "menos vento em Lisboa" on Tuesday night, when the warning in force said gusts up to 120 km/h, and 140 in the most exposed places, from 12:00 to 21:00 on Wednesday, unchanged since Tuesday at 07:18. Some seven hours after the headlines, IPMA lowered the level to orange and dropped the 140; the 120 km/h is still warned, from 09:00.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: this desk, setting a headline beside a warning

claims.text: What an IPMA meteorologist said aloud sits between the two: an entry further south and the strongest winds, if they form, probably south of Lisbon; and "isto ainda atinge a zona de Lisboa". IPMA has put neither sentence in writing.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: this desk, setting the spoken line beside IPMA's written channels

claims.text: Nothing measured yet can test any of this: the orange wind warning and the red rain warning both begin at 09:00 on Wednesday, and the observations we hold end before it.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's stations and the airport's METAR, as read

supports.note: The newest station hour held, as it stands at each build.
The airport's newest report, as it stands at each build.
A tripwire: when the station hour labelled 12:00 arrives, this sentence is behind the data and is retold.

claims.text: So far the strongest gust in the airport's reports we hold is 36 knots (67 km/h), on Tuesday at 11:00, and the data room's list of airport gusts above the gust warned for their hour, kept from 05:00 on Wednesday, is empty.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Lisbon airport's METAR (issued by IPMA, read through NOAA's Aviation Weather)

supports.note: A tripwire: the data room lists here every airport gust from Wed 05:00 above the gust warned for that hour. Empty at this read.

claims.text: The meteorologist has written down in advance what Wednesday's observations at the airport would show either way: "LPPT veer through SW to W with strongest S gusts before the pressure minimum = centre passed north; back through E to N = passed south".
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: a test set in advance, not a result
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.expect: LPPT veer through SW to W with strongest S gusts before the pressure minimum = centre passed north; back through E to N = passed south

claims.text: Our meteorologist's reading of the change, written at 07:45: it is consistent with what IPMA's forecasters said on radio at 22:35 (the worst further south); IPMA now judges Lisbon's gusts at up to 120 km/h, not 140. In the analysis's words: "Not a 'storm is over': orange means dangerous weather; red rain still stands 09:00-18:00." Its guidance for a headline is now: "IPMA lowers Lisbon's wind warning to orange (gusts to 120 km/h, 09:00-21:00); the red rain warning (09:00-18:00) stands".
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: an analysis of a fact; which side of Lisbon the centre passes is still unsettled in it
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

contains: Not a 'storm is over': orange means dangerous weather; red rain still stands 09:00-18:00.

supports.expect: IPMA lowers Lisbon's wind warning to orange (gusts to 120 km/h, 09:00-21:00); the red rain warning (09:00-18:00) stands

record.what: First telling, on the data read at 01:51:55 UTC: 26 sentences. Lisbon's red wind and red rain warnings stand; no communiqué no. 3; three models in the data room disagree; nothing observed yet tests it.

Checked against the read of 02:22:46 UTC. Nothing moved at IPMA: the same warnings for Lisbon, the communiqué still no. 2. Nothing moved in the three models. The airport's latest report is now 02:00 (wind from 200° at 5 knots, 1006 hPa), so the two sentences on the observations were retold.

The hypothesis layer retold from the meteorologist's re-weighing of 02:35 UTC (analysis.md 7b, row s-1111T0229), which followed this story's note that an input had moved. Before: "very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00, more likely just south", confidence medium; headline guidance "IPMA's forecasters expect the strongest winds south of Lisbon; Lisbon's red warnings stand". Now: which side of Lisbon the centre passes is unsettled (low); very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00 (medium); "'less wind for Lisbon' is not supported". Nothing changed at IPMA: the red warnings stand. Row supports now show our own capture first where the evidence section holds one.

Checked against the read of 02:38:08 UTC: nothing moved at IPMA or in the models. The two sentences on the observations no longer quote the airport's newest half-hourly report (it was 02:00: wind from 200° at 5 knots, 1006 hPa); they now say what holds until something measurable happens, with tripwires on the first station hour at 12:00 and on the first gust above the warned gust.

Checked against the read of 03:23:31 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2, the models unchanged. One sentence added from a new timeline row (s-1111T0328): RTP's 03:00 bulletin title puts the shift south under IPMA's name again; IPMA has still written nothing new. Three supports now name the 01:29 re-read by its time (the list of re-reads had grown).

Checked against the read of 04:23:17 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2. One model moved: Open-Meteo's strongest mean wind was 20.6 km/h (gust 52.6) at 14:00 from the north-east; it is now 18.7 km/h (gust 53.6) at 10:00 from the south-south-west. MET Norway's values and IPMA's hourly model are as before. The three still disagree.

Checked against the read of 05:22:49 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2. A new airport forecast (issued 05:00): the 45-knot gust group now runs 09:00 to 18:00 (the 23:00 issue, which this story quoted as "weaker at 23:00 than at 17:00", ended it at 16:00); the 30% chance of 58-knot gusts is kept. MET Norway re-stamped its run with the same values.

Checked against the read of 06:25:17 UTC: IPMA's red rain (09:00 to 18:00) and red wind (12:00 to 21:00) for Lisbon unchanged. Open-Meteo's values moved. Before: strongest mean 18.7 km/h and strongest gust 53.6 km/h, both at 10:00, from the south-south-west; 16.1 km/h at 14:00. Now: 19.4 km/h at 10:00 and 50 km/h at 11:00, from the south; 17.6 km/h at 14:00.

The top of the story changed. Before: IPMA had sent no message that lowered, shortened or lifted a Lisbon warning; red wind 12:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h and 140 in the most exposed places. Now: at 07:16:30 on Wednesday IPMA lowered the wind warning to orange, 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h (row s-1111T0738); red rain unchanged; IPMA's open-data feed still showed red wind at 07:38; the meteorologist's reading of 07:45 added. Supports for the red wind warning now point at the kept CAP message, since the replaced warning leaves the feed.

The box at the top is now drawn from both of IPMA's channels, as the front page draws it: the newest message for each kind of weather, and what the open-data feed still lists where the two differ (before, it was drawn from the open data alone and showed red wind after IPMA's 07:16 message had lowered it to orange). The supports for Lisbon's red rain warning (09:00 to 18:00) now point at IPMA's kept message (PO-10-6290, sent 10 Nov 21:23) rather than the open-data list, which drops a warning when it ends; no sentence changed.

Retold on the read of 08:45:09 UTC. Before: IPMA's open-data feed still showed red wind (07:38). Now: the feed has the orange warning, 66 to 88 minutes after the message (row s-1111T0844). Before: IPMA's hourly model had Wednesday's strongest mean wind at 23.4 km/h at 20:00; now 40 km/h at 14:00, from the south. Before: MET Norway 58.3 km/h and 987.7 hPa at 15:00; now 55.1 km/h and 988.8 hPa at 15:00. The comparison of the three models follows. The warning windows open at 09:00; nothing measured inside them is in this telling.
